newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices mixed in Friday trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices mixed in Friday trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices were mixed Friday, with a large sale raising the values of light Line 63 crude while a decrease in postings trimmed the value of heavy California crudes, traders said.
Traders said Koch sold a 7,000 barrel-per-day (API) contract of Line 63 (28 API) to Atlantic Richfield midweek for delivery over the next two months.
The contract sold for $3.05 cents under bellwether West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude, traders said.

Sales of Alaska North Slope crude -- the regional benchmark -- remained stagnant, with key buyers in the Pacific Northwest oversupplied with gasoline and unable to pay BP's current offer of $1.85 under WTI.
U.S. Oil, Tosco Corp, and Shell Oil were heard cuttinng back the amount of crude processed the past month.
Buyers were seen bidding at much bigger discounts, one at $2.50, to the current market value of $2.16 under.
With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude oil with higher cash prices.
But with its discount rising, from about $3.40 under WTI to $3.05, outright prices for Line 63 also rpse, hitting the $16.24/16.43 a barrel range.
Meanwhile, Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- fell after major oil companies lowered postings late Thursday and Friday.
